name: destructive-arming-reset-by-another-intent
description: A destructive request is armed by one Approve, then the person does something else (any other intent). That disarms it, so the next Approve arms the request again instead of allowing it.
reason: Two presses only confirm when they belong together. If anything happens between them, a later stray Approve (minutes later, or a misheard word) must not complete a confirmation the person has moved on from.
source: Epic #92 rule 'the armed state resets on any other intent'; ticket #116; DESIGN.md v2.2 §C (as amended by #116); AppState.handle

script.text: Throw away my last three commits
